title: feat(plugin-auth, platform-objects): an SSO provider maps the email and name a sign-in resolves to, and a refused SAML response names its cause
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBDE67gQzDMEEhPfYg79Xcjb)_

Part of #32086

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Claim by `domain:server#4` (6764573689), seat rulings in claim amendments 6764693228 (split: this PR is items 2 and 3) and 6764776096 (the two dogfood route classifications). Item 1 (the third-party-initiated OIDC door) follows in its own PR under ruling A on #32150 (6764924025).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：SSO 提供方可以映射“登录解析成谁”：SAML 的邮箱、名、姓、显示名属性，OIDC 的邮箱、姓名 claim。注册 SAML 表单新增四个字段，已有提供方新增“查看/编辑属性映射”两个动作和两个平台管理员桥接。SAML 的 `Invalid SAML response` 拒绝现在在 `error_description` 里给出四种原因之一（证书轮换、IdP 失败状态、未签名、Issuer 不符）。
- 为什么改：Okta 的 `name`、Entra ID 的 claim URI 与厂商默认属性名不同，这些用户只能以 NameID 命名，且平台里没有任何地方能改映射。IdP 证书轮换后管理员只看到一句不透明的拒绝，无从排查。
- 风险与回滚：接受或拒绝的判定不变，只在厂商已拒绝后改写 `error_description`（`error=saml_error` 不变）。编辑映射时未填的成员保留，组 claim 等其余成员原样保留。存量数据就是厂商原生的 `mapping` 字段，回滚即 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-refusal-cause.ts`（诊断规则），然后 `register-sso-provider.ts` 末尾的 “The attribute mapping” 一节。
- 两分钟验证：`cd packages/plugins/plugin-auth && pnpm exec vitest run src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts -t 32086`，预期 11 条全过（真实 samlify IdP 走完四种拒绝原因和 Okta、Entra 映射）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。cloud 侧 AuthProxyPlugin 是否挂载两个新桥接已记为范围外发现。

## What changes

**Attribute mapping (item 2).** `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 reads a SAML user's email from attribute `mapping.email` (default `email`, else the NameID) and the name from `mapping.firstName` + `mapping.lastName` (defaults `givenName`, `surname`), else `mapping.name` (default `displayName`), else the NameID. OIDC reads `mapping.email` / `mapping.name` (defaults `email`, `name`). Nothing in the platform could set those members, so an Okta user (full name in `name`) or an Entra ID user (claim URIs) was named after the NameID.

- `register-sso-provider.ts`:
  - `runRegisterSamlProviderFromForm` reads four new flat fields, `mapEmail`, `mapFirstName`, `mapLastName`, `mapName` (trimmed; blank leaves the vendor default), into `samlConfig.mapping` beside `extraFields.groups`.
  - New section "The attribute mapping": `mappingWithAttributes`, `attributeMappingOf`, `SSO_ATTRIBUTE_MAPPING_MEMBERS`, and the two bridges `runShowSsoAttributeMapping` / `runSetSsoAttributeMapping`, built on the groups-claim bridges' pattern (system read seam for the `internal` blob, re-dispatch to the vendor's `/sso/update-provider` with the stored mapping and only the given members changed, only the inner status comes back).
  - Set semantics, matching what the console's param dialog sends (only touched params, a cleared field as `''`): absent or `null` keeps a member, a string sets it, a blank string removes it (default again). A body naming no member is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` "Nothing to change"; a non-string member is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; `firstName` / `lastName` on an OIDC provider is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` naming the one claim it reads; an unknown provider is `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`; a vendor refusal keeps its status with the standard code for it and a message that carries none of the vendor body.
  - The answer is exactly `{ providerId, protocol, email, firstName, lastName, name }`.
- `auth-plugin.ts`: mounts `POST {basePath}/admin/sso/get-attribute-mapping` and `.../set-attribute-mapping`, `gateAdmin` first (ADR-0068 D4), beside the groups-claim pair.
- `auth-route-ledger.ts`: two rows, `objectstack-mount`, `server-only`, `requires: 'sso'`.
- `platform-objects` `sys-sso-provider.object.ts`: the four `register_saml_provider` params (help text names the Okta and Entra ID attribute names); new actions `show_sso_attribute_mapping` and `edit_sso_attribute_mapping` (platform-admin standing, `list_item` + `record_header`, `resultDialog`; no `ai` block on the edit because the email member decides which account a sign-in links to). Translations regenerated and translated in all ten locales (only the placeholders, which are attribute names, stay source copies, as the groups claim's does).
- Dogfood: the two new routes classified beside the groups-claim pair in `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal` and `admin-platform-admin-standing` (amendment 6764776096).

**SAML refusal causes (item 3).** The vendor wraps samlify's `parseLoginResponse` in a bare `catch`, logs `SAML response validation failed` and redirects `error=saml_error&error_description=Invalid SAML response` for every samlify rejection.

- New `sso-saml-refusal-cause.ts`: after the vendor has answered that exact redirect, the posted `SAMLResponse` is read once more against the provider's stored signing configuration (`idpMetadata.metadata` XML when present, else `idpMetadata.cert ?? cert`, one or a list, and `idpMetadata.entityID`, as the vendor's `createIdP` builds its IdP), in samlify 2.13.1's order:
  1. `saml_idp_status_not_success`: top-level `StatusCode` present and not `...:status:Success` (samlify `checkStatus`, before signatures);
  2. `saml_response_unsigned`: no Response or Assertion `Signature`, and no `EncryptedAssertion`;
  3. `saml_signing_certificate_mismatch`: the first signature samlify checks embeds an `X509Certificate` not among the configured ones, both normalised as samlify's `normalizeCerString` does (samlify's `ERROR_UNMATCH_CERTIFICATE_DECLARATION_IN_METADATA`, the certificate rotation case);
  4. `saml_issuer_mismatch`: that certificate is configured and the Assertion `Issuer` is not the configured IdP entity id (`ERR_UNMATCH_ISSUER`).
  Anything else is unclassified and the vendor's answer stands byte for byte: XML the vendor's own `XMLValidator` rejects, a missing status, a signature without an embedded certificate, an encrypted assertion, a wrapping shape samlify refuses first, or a response whose certificate and issuer both match (broken signature, expired assertion). Only `error_description` changes; `error=saml_error`, the target and every header are kept, and one `warn` line `{ providerId, protocol: 'saml', cause }` is written.
- `auth-manager.ts` `runSsoCallback`: one hook in the SAML closure wraps the vendor run in `runSsoSamlRefusalCauseScope`, reading the stored `samlConfig` through the vendor's own adapter (`ssoProvider` by `providerId`, as `findSAMLProvider` reads it). `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.ts` changes only its header note that SAML causes waited on the vendor.
- `fast-xml-parser` `5.10.1` (the parser and options the vendor already uses) becomes a direct dependency of plugin-auth: `package.json` and the lockfile importer entry only, no new package fetched.

Docs: `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` gains the four register fields, "Map the user's email and name" (with the Okta and Entra ID attribute table) and "Why a SAML sign-in was refused" (the four causes); the OIDC section's "SAML refusals do not name their cause yet" now points there.

## Tests

- `register-sso-provider.test.ts`: the SAML form sends each named attribute trimmed beside the groups attribute, omits blank ones, and sends no mapping when none is named (CONTROL); through the REAL route, the form's mapping is stored exactly as the register door stores the same mapping (Entra claim URIs). Bridges: show answers each protocol's members; set sends update-provider the stored mapping with only the given members changed (`extraFields`, `emailVerified`, `image`, `id` kept) and answers it read back; blank removes, absent and `null` keep; nothing-to-change, OIDC first/last name, non-text members and a missing `providerId` are `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with nothing written; unknown provider `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` on both; no answer (show, set, vendor refusal echoing a secret and the certificate) carries any other stored member.
- `admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts`, `auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: both bridges run the platform-admin gate (401 / 403 with code), and the ledger rows match the mounts.
- New `sso-saml-refusal-cause.test.ts`: every rule on hand-written envelopes (check order, first-signature rule, `#text` issuers, PEM normalisation, metadata XML shared and `use="signing"` certificates, 13 unclassified shapes), and the scope (only the opaque refusal is rewritten, relative targets stay relative, headers kept, JSON bodies read, unreadable or failing configuration reads leave the vendor answer as is).
- `sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts` (shared harness, new top-level describes per ruling 6583487846): a real AuthManager refusing real samlify responses lands each of the four causes on the error page with `error=saml_error` and one warn line, signing nobody in; CONTROLs: a broken signature under the known certificate and issuer stays `Invalid SAML response` with no cause line, a valid response still signs in; a PEM-armoured configured certificate is the same certificate; adding the rotated certificate as a list lets the same sign-in through; no subject or certificate in the redirect or the line. Mapping at sign-in: unmapped, an Okta `name` attribute is ignored and the user is named after the NameID; mapped `name`, the user is "Mia Chen"; Entra claim URIs map the email (over an opaque NameID) and given name + surname.
- `platform-objects.test.ts` / `platform-admin-affordance-standing.test.ts`: the two new actions carry the platform-admin standing.

## Acceptance notes

- Item 3 decides nothing: it runs only after the vendor's refusal is final, does no cryptography, and reads only the envelope, the embedded certificate and the issuer, compared with the IdP's public certificate and entity id. The answer is the same for every account (no user lookup has happened).
- `saml_issuer_mismatch` carries the residual ambiguity named at step 0: without verifying the signature it cannot be told from "configured certificate, broken signature, wrong issuer". An IdP holding the configured key signs validly, so the label is the right one in practice.
- The vendor's own `SAML response validation failed` error line is left as written (holding it would mean a second hook in the shared log sink); the cause is one `warn` line beside it.
- `SSO_SAML_REFUSAL_CAUSES` is exported from its module but not from the package entry (the entry is outside this card's surface); noted as a finding.
- The register OIDC form is unchanged: it already maps `email` / `name`, and the edit bridge serves OIDC providers for those two members (seat ruling).

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run`: 256 files, 4650 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects exec vitest run`: 120 files, 1936 passed.
- `packages/qa/dogfood` `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal` + `admin-platform-admin-standing` on the built stack: 15 passed.
- `typecheck` + `check:test-typecheck` for plugin-auth and platform-objects, dogfood `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0. Root eslint on every touched file: exit 0.
- `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` (none new), `check:i18n-stale-fill`: OK.
- 18 negative pins ablated through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: each red under its mutation, restored, `git diff HEAD` empty. The derived `dispatch-gates --commands` set was run on the final head under `os-verify-lock` and reconciled with `--ran`; the record is in the card's report.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (not touched)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (root eslint on every touched file, exit 0)
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request. (this card ships as two PRs by seat ruling 6764693228; this is the first)
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. (not touched)
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English. (except the `维护者速读` block the dispatch asks for)
